Synopsis:
    Gaza farmers are rebuilding a local seed bank destroyed during Israel's military campaign, preserving native crop varieties amid severe land restrictions. With ~70% of pre-war farmland under Israeli military control or inaccessible due to the Yellow Line buffer zone, farmers are cultivating the remaining ~25-30% of Gaza's territory. Import restrictions tightened through 2025 made local heirloom seeds a critical survival resource. The agricultural sector, which once supported 560,000 livelihoods, remains devastated, with the seed bank effort described as "a drop in the ocean" relative to actual needs. Ongoing Israeli military presence near farmland continues to pose physical danger to farmers.
